narrative:
The model estimates a 69% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your background.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest influence pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while the rest had six or more years. This limited tenure appears to signal higher turnover risk to the system.

The fact that you have received other job offers while at the company was the second most important factor, pushing the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model predicted would stay had not received outside opportunities.

Your placement in the “other” business sector also contributed toward predicting that you would leave, though less strongly than the first two factors. Only about 22% of employees expected to stay work in this broad category, compared with higher shares in medical or education fields.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you directly, exploring ways to build your experience internally, and understanding what might make you want to stay. You may wish to reflect on whether the external opportunities you’ve received better match your long-term aims.
